summary: The always-visible way to end a running agent. Not optional, and not behind a menu.
useWhen: anything runs long enough that a person might want it to stop — a generation, a tool chain, a batch job
the run was started by the user and is still going

useInstead.when: the action is instant and there is nothing to interrupt
you are asking permission before something happens rather than ending something already happening
the thing to undo has already finished
useInstead.why: an undo affordance belongs with the confirmation of what was done

sm.use: inside a toolbar or beside an inline activity row

lg.use: a full-width run surface where stopping is the primary available action

guarantees: the control keeps its place while stopping — it relabels and disables rather than disappearing, so the layout does not move under the pointer
the transition to stopping is announced once through a polite live region, because the label change alone is only heard if the button happens to hold focus
`stopOnEscape` ignores Escape raised inside a dialog, so closing a modal never cancels a background run
requires: keeping it rendered and visible for the whole run — a stop control that scrolls away or hides in an overflow menu is the failure this component exists to prevent
notes: It does not stop anything. It reports intent; aborting the request and settling the state is the caller's. A stop that resolves optimistically while output keeps arriving lies about the one guarantee the user is relying on.

antiPatterns.dont: putting the stop control in an overflow menu
antiPatterns.why: a user who cannot reach it is watching the agent, not supervising it

antiPatterns.dont: disabling it while the run is going
antiPatterns.why: the only correct disabled state is `isStopping` — after the request, never before

antiPatterns.dont: unmounting it the moment it is pressed
antiPatterns.why: the run is usually still going, and a control that vanishes leaves the user unsure the press registered
stopping is normal and repeatable; red teaches hesitation about the one control that must never be hesitated over

antiPatterns.dont: `stopOnEscape` on a page with modals over the run
antiPatterns.why: Escape already means dismiss to every overlay in this system
